title: Stretch and secure fabric in an embroidery hoop
instruction: Stretch the fabric in the embroidery hoop and secure it, ready to stitch.
context: Prepare fabric for hand embroidery: remove slack in several directions, then tighten the ordinary hoop screw so the unsupported working area stays flat after release.
setup: A 130 mm beechwood embroidery hoop with a brass M3 thumb screw is held horizontal by three wooden rim supports, 45 mm above the table. A 240 mm diameter piece of plain woven cotton (140-180 g/m2) is already loosely seated between the rings, with its centre 8-12 mm below the rim; its outer edge hangs freely. The screw starts one quarter-turn short of its finger-tight setting. The centre has no backing or pins. Both hands start open. README gives the low-cost support layout and repeatable reset.
scoring: Score the final state. 1.0: fabric is retained around at least 95% of the rim, the screw is tightened, and the central 96 mm working area stays within 5 mm of the rim plane, with at most 5 mm peak-to-valley variation, for 3 seconds after both hands release. 0.75 for that result before release/hold completion; 0.5 if retained and tightened but still too slack; 0.25 if at least half the rim retains the cloth but less than 95%, or if fully retained and drawn within 5 mm but not tightened. Otherwise 0. Any tear or pulled-out fabric invalidates the result. Use a ruler, straightedge, photographs and the video.
fidelity: Native YAM arms and cameras. Cotton is a flexible spring mesh with gravity, in-plane stretch/shear and weak bending. Only the hoop annulus retains it; material can slide through the loose rim. Measured screw rotation increases rim friction. The centre is unsupported. Finger captures, fixture contact, screw friction and tear thresholds are reduced, uncalibrated approximations; no scripted flattening or interior pins.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0; scripted demo: 1.0. Dream completed with 33 server sessions after expiry recoveries.
reset_notes: Use the same cotton stock, unstarched and dry. Loosen the screw, lift out and recenter the cloth, then reseat with 8-12 mm centre sag measured with a straightedge. Set the screw a quarter-turn back from the recorded finger-tight mark. Reject damaged or permanently stretched cloth. No needle or stitching is needed.
